ask_public: • No agent access: AI agents and API tokens that act for you are refused. Ask and meaning alerts are features of EarWitness itself. They do not let any outside agent or token reach your workspace.

While the pilot runs, we keep your sign-in ID and email, your sessions, the demo content, and what you create in the workspace. It is hosted on Hetzner Cloud in Nuremberg, Germany. Questions you ask, earlier answers in the same chat, meaning-alert sentences, the passages a word search finds for them, and brand names from the collection are also processed by Meta (Meta's Model API), possibly outside the EU, including in the United States. Meta also gets nearby transcript text when the model asks for it, each passage's show, episode, time and whether it is inside an ad, and the question a brand button asks for you. EarWitness sends no name, email or account ID. Do not type personal information into a question. Our deletion limits cover our own servers, not copies Meta keeps.
• Your Ask questions and answers, with copies of the passages the search found for them. In the app, only you can see your Ask questions and answers. They are deleted with the workspace.

• A deletion record stays, during the pilot and after it: request records, removed account IDs and emails, and the signed rights records and addenda. It holds no transcript text. It has no set end date.

These pages load only their own text, styles, fonts, script and images, all served by EarWitness. Nothing loads from other sites: no outside fonts, scripts, trackers or images. Show cover art and brand logos are copies we host; they belong to their owners and are shown only to name the show or brand. In the pilot, the app contacts one outside service: Meta's Model API, when you use Ask or a meaning alert. No outside program can connect to your workspace.
• Each workspace holds one collection under one signed rights record and, for Ask and meaning alerts, one signed addendum. The app allows only the uses they cover.

A result shows what was said in a specific episode. It is not proof of ad spend, reach or delivery. A search with no result does not prove an ad never ran. Some campaign checks say "Not enough data"; treat those as unknown. Answers from Ask and matches from meaning alerts are written by an AI model and can be wrong. Check each cited passage. Check anything important against the original episode.

methodology_public.old: The four steps
methodology_public.new:
How we find ads

  1. We turn each episode’s audio into a transcript with timestamps.
  2. Software marks the parts that sound like an ad.
  3. Software names the brand from the words it hears. If it isn’t sure, the ad shows as “Brand not identified”.
  4. Each ad links to its passage in the transcript. Some ads also keep a short audio clip; we don’t keep the full episode audio.

Start and end times are approximate, and a found ad can be wrong. We can also miss ads, so a count is the ads we found, not every ad that ran. Use “Report a mistake” on the ad’s page.

Using EarWitness

methodology_public.old: • Discover. Search the covered collection for spoken passages matching scoped criteria.
methodology_public.new: • Search. Search what was said in the shows we cover.

methodology_public.old: • Inspect a source-pinned passage. Open the exact source, interval, nearby context, and provenance — not a summary of the market.
methodology_public.new: • Open the passage. See the exact words, the episode, the time, the text around it, and where the record came from.

methodology_public.old: • Compare observations. Place two pinned passages side by side with their dates. Different wording is an observation, not proof of replacement.
methodology_public.new: • Compare. Put two brands side by side.

methodology_public.old: • Save research. Keep excerpts, queries, and bookmarks as durable records with their captured revisions.
methodology_public.new: • Save. Keep passages, searches and bookmarks. A saved passage keeps the transcript version you saved.

methodology_public.old: • Product-assisted judgments are working notes, not independent accuracy labels.
methodology_public.new: • Our own checks on ads are working notes, not accuracy scores.

methodology_public.old: • A source digest compares bytes; it is not a legal or authenticity seal.
methodology_public.new: • A file fingerprint shows only that two copies match. It is not a legal or authenticity seal.

methodology_public.old: Where audio, timing or requirements are missing, we say so. A matching passage is an observation from the covered collection — see Coverage.
methodology_public.new: Where audio, timing or requirements are missing, we say so. A match is something heard in the shows we cover, nothing more — see Coverage.

methodology_public.old: Every count in the workspace counts records the collection holds: episodes, passages, and observations from fetched sources. These numbers say nothing about podcasts outside the collection.
methodology_public.new: Every count in the app counts what we hold: episodes, passages and ads from the shows we cover. It says nothing about other podcasts.

methodology_public.old: A search with no matches establishes only that nothing matching was found in the covered collection. It does not establish that no brand mention exists anywhere.
methodology_public.new: A search with no matches means nothing matched in the shows we cover. It does not mean the brand was never mentioned anywhere.

methodology_public.old: Sources without a known publication date are labeled with their unknown date whenever no date restriction is active. They are not silently dropped and not silently grouped with dated results.
methodology_public.new: Episodes with no known publish date are marked “Date unknown”. When no date filter is on, they still show, with that label.

methodology_public.old: Dynamic insertion can change later recordings: a source fetched again later may carry different bytes and a new revision. Saved pins keep their captured revision; the current transcript may differ.
methodology_public.new: Some ads are inserted when an episode is downloaded, so a later download can hold different ads. A saved passage keeps the transcript version you saved; the current transcript may differ.

methodology_public.old: Historical fixture or evaluation counts are not current quality claims and are not quoted here. Treat any number you see in the workspace as a stored-collection count with its displayed scope and revision.
methodology_public.new: We don’t quote test or accuracy numbers here; past test results are not quality claims. A number in the app counts what we hold, for the filters shown.

methodology_public.old: Excerpts, queries and bookmarks stay as durable research with their captured revisions. A frozen report downloads as the same bytes every time.
methodology_public.new: Save passages, searches and bookmarks. A saved passage keeps the transcript version you saved. A final report downloads exactly the same every time.
